artifacts.summary: All seven phases COMPLETED: .gate-lock bounded-wait fail-open mutex added to task-lock.sh, wired into tests/run-all.sh and verify-deploy.sh's Gate 8, with a 15-case fixture suite, documented contract, redeploy confirmed byte-identical, and a 37/38 complete gate-set run with the sole deviation fully attributed to evidence.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a repo-scoped .gate-lock bounded-wait, fail-open mutex to task-lock.sh and bracketed tests/run-all.sh's top level and verify-deploy.sh's Gate 8 with it, so two concurrent sessions' full gate-set batteries serialize instead of contending for the same cores. All seven plan phases closed [COMPLETED]: 15/15 fixture cases pass against the real mechanism (serialization, non-vacuousness, stale-reclaim, nested invocation, fail-open at both call sites, verdict identity); the contract is documented in batch-orchestration-guardrails.md; the deploy is regenerated and confirmed byte-identical to source; and the complete gate set passes 37/38 against the explicit source-store target, with the sole failure traced to a foreign, out-of-scope uncommitted mutation in a file this task never touched. A genuine integration defect (VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED read before its own unconditional export, inside gate8_run()) was found and fixed during implementation and is documented in the plan body and summary.

memory_candidates.content: When wiring a bounded-wait/fail-open coordination bracket into a script that ALREADY carries its own unconditional self-nesting-guard export near its top (e.g. `export RUN_ALL_NESTED=1` or `export VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED=1`, set unconditionally so a LATER nested invocation sees it as 1), do not check that live variable directly inside the new bracket -- by the time the bracket's own code runs, the export has already fired, so the check always reads "1" regardless of whether THIS invocation was actually nested at entry. Capture a `*_WAS_NESTED_AT_ENTRY="${VAR:-}"` snapshot immediately BEFORE the pre-existing unconditional export, and test the captured value instead. Confirmed as a real, live-reproducible defect (not theoretical): a forced acquire showed the wrong process as the mutex owner until fixed.

git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check silently drops any files_touched path not present in the task's own declared file_scope (fail-open drop-and-warn, by design) -- it does not refuse the commit, it just omits that one path with a WARNING line. If that WARNING is not read carefully at the time a phase closes, the dropped file can sit uncommitted for multiple subsequent phases without being noticed via a casual git status glance (since other unrelated dirty files in a shared multi-session tree provide cover). Before trusting a phase-closing commit as complete, either (a) declare every file you expect to touch in file_scope up front, or (b) explicitly re-check `git status --porcelain` against your own known-touched-file list right after each commit, not just the commit's own summary line.

A synthetic test fixture that needs a deployed sibling script (e.g. task-lock.sh at $WORKDIR/.claude/scripts/task-lock.sh, resolved via common_repo_root's 2-levels-up convention) to be DISCOVERABLE from a source-store-shaped fixture root must nest its fake 'extensions root' exactly as many directory levels under $WORKDIR as the real repository nests agent-system/extensions under the repo root (two levels: agent-system/extensions). A shallower one-level fixture (e.g. $WORKDIR/exts/core, fine for fixtures that never need this resolution) makes any 'N levels up from EXTENSIONS_ROOT' arithmetic land one level too high, silently failing to find the fixture's own deployed-script copy.
